response.markdown_report:
The best first step is a paired, rank-based diagnostic adapter that tests reliance on recent evidence while preserving the benchmark and SASRec architecture. No ranking improvement has yet been measured.

**Insights from the starting point**

1. Broad relevance can obscure specific interests. Recent and repeated interactions offer observable evidence, but cannot establish current intent.
2. Existing margins depend on score scale and sampled negatives. Paired target ranks make perturbation comparisons easier to interpret.
3. The stable adapter already exposes encoding and scoring. It can support behavioral probes without changing inference or assuming unavailable metadata.

**Insights from related work**

1. Excessive recency bias can reduce accuracy [1]. Recent-history dependence therefore needs comparison with older-history and random controls.
2. Sampled evaluation can change model comparisons [2]. Diagnostic candidate sets must remain fixed across perturbations, and their results must remain separate from benchmark selection.
3. Selective prediction distinguishes asserted judgments from uncertainty [3]. Compatibility audits should similarly abstain when titles and descriptions lack explicit evidence; this transfer remains a methodological proposal.

**Framework and directions**

| Direction | Existing signal | Proposed extension | Interpretation limit |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ranking reliability | Raw margins | Paired target-rank changes | Candidate-dependent |
| Temporal reliance | Unmodified histories | Matched deletion and shuffle controls | Sensitivity, not intent |
| Evidence quality | Qualitative feedback | Supported judgment or abstention | Requires annotation |

**Candidate ideas**

Scores are originality/potential/difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

- **Paired history perturbation adapter — 4/8/3.** Originality: useful combination, but familiar probes. Potential: reusable across architectures, but diagnostic validity needs testing. Difficulty: existing hooks suffice, but padding needs care. Builds on [1,2].
- **Candidate-set disagreement audit — 3/7/4.** Originality: combines established comparisons, but adds little theory. Potential: exposes sampling dependence, but cannot replace pinned evaluation. Difficulty: sampled ranks are easy, but catalog scans cost time [2].
- **Evidence-backed compatibility audit — 6/6/7.** Originality: transfers selective judgment to recommendation, but abstention is established. Potential: explains unsupported recommendations, but annotation may not predict HR@10. Difficulty: uses available text, but reliable rules require substantial checking [3].

**Selected algorithm**

At 0% progress, implement the first idea. On fixed training prefixes, compare unchanged histories with equal-count recent, oldest, and seeded random deletions; additionally shuffle earlier items while preserving the last item. Recompute features and score identical candidates. Report paired target-rank changes, top-10 overlap, sample counts, and category-specific results with an equal-weight macro summary.

These are in-sample sensitivity measurements because the trained model may have seen the targets. They neither demonstrate generalization nor justify inferred ownership or dislikes. Preserve `DiagnosisProbe(view, device)`, both required methods, model mode, and explicit metric definitions. Select checkpoints only using pinned macro validation HR@10.

References: [1] https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.09722; [2] https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.13045; [3] https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.15610.

idea.description: Extend the architecture-aware DiagnosisProbe with controlled, paired history perturbations and rank-based measurements to distinguish recent-evidence reliance from broad historical dependence.
idea.motivation: Qualitative feedback identifies recommendations supported by broad associations rather than recent, specific evidence. Existing embedding and margin probes do not measure this dependence. A small diagnostic extension is feasible at the initial research stage without claiming that stronger recency dependence necessarily improves recommendations.
idea.implementation_notes: Keep DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], all four dataset routes, baseline splits, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, and the existing predictor writer. No model or inference change is required. Store diagnostic outputs beneath the trial directory. Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Access the trained module through view.model and scoring through the compatibility hooks. Use fixed training examples and unique candidate negatives excluding padding, target, and observed prefix items; report eligible-example counts. Right-align compacted sequences using the original padding convention and extract the last non-padding feature. Set deletion count so at least one history item remains. Define target rank as 1 plus the number of candidates scoring strictly above the target, and document ties. Restore the original model mode after diagnostics. Label all training-target results as in-sample; aggregate within category before equal-weight averaging. Report shuffle variability and paired user-bootstrap intervals only when enough distinct users are available. Skip unsupported probes explicitly rather than inventing results. Keep diagnostic work bounded and charge its GPU time to the shared budget. Compatibility, immediate-choice acceptance, and simulator traits remain unmeasured.
idea.pseudocode:
run_full_diagnosis(train_loader):
    save view.model.training; switch to eval
    select a bounded, seeded set of training-prefix/next-item examples
    for each eligible example:
        construct one fixed candidate set containing target and 99 unique negatives
        score unchanged prefix; record target rank and top-10 IDs
        k = min(configured_deletions, prefix_length - 1)
        construct recent-k, oldest-k, and seeded random-k deletions
        construct earlier-item shuffle preserving the last item
        for each variant:
            compact and right-pad/left-pad exactly as the baseline requires
            encode through view.log2feats; select last valid feature
            score the same candidates through view.predict_score
            record paired rank change and top-10 overlap
    aggregate per category, then equally across all four categories
    restore model mode in a finally block
    return {'metrics': measured_results, 'metric_definitions': definitions_and_limits}

diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis):
    embed measured metrics and definitions
    request evidence-linked findings and explicit uncertainty
    prohibit claims about validation gains, current intent, or unavailable traits

originality.positive: Combines architecture-compatible hooks, matched temporal controls, and rank-based evidence in a reusable adapter.
originality.negative: Perturbation tests and paired ranking comparisons are established techniques; novelty lies mainly in their disciplined integration.

future_potential.positive: Provides a reusable way to test whether later architecture or loss changes alter dependence on recent and repeated evidence.
future_potential.negative: Sensitivity measurements may not predict pinned validation improvement and cannot identify user intent causally.

code_difficulty.positive: Uses existing encoder and scorer hooks without introducing additional models or external data.
code_difficulty.negative: Correct padding, candidate eligibility, feature selection, and paired aggregation require careful implementation.

related_work.title: Oh and Cho (2024): excessive recency bias in recommendation, as described in the supplied research results
contributions: Motivates separating useful recent evidence from excessive recency dependence.
Supports including older-history and random controls when interpreting temporal perturbations.
limitations: Does not establish the best recency treatment for these four Amazon datasets.
Does not validate the proposed diagnostic adapter.

related_work.title: Sampled recommendation evaluation comparison, as described in the supplied research results
contributions: Highlights that sampled evaluation can change model comparisons.
Motivates fixed candidates for paired diagnostics and explicit separation from the pinned benchmark.
limitations: Does not make a diagnostic candidate set equivalent to full-catalog ranking.
Does not justify modifying the host evaluator.

related_work.title: ReCoVERR (2024)
contributions: Provides an example of evidence gathering and selective prediction.
Motivates recording uncertainty separately from asserted compatibility judgments.
limitations: Studies visual question answering rather than recommendation.
Its reported benefits do not establish recommendation accuracy or compatibility-audit validity.
